before: A range view describes iteration rather than eagerly creating a new vector. std::views::filter keeps values satisfying a predicate; std::views::transform computes a value from each kept element. | composes these adaptors.
The for loop traverses the pipeline: filter values greater than 1, then multiply each by 10. The underlying vector remains 1,2,3. This example does not modify it while a view is being traversed.
This view refers to the named vector, which outlives traversal. Do not return this view from a function if its local vector would be destroyed. Avoid assuming views are cached result collections.

Expected output or behavior: 20 30 
. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Keep the filter but change the transform to x+10 and predict the values before running. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A view describes how to visit data. It does not immediately build a new vector of results. This is called lazy work: results are produced as the loop asks for them.
std::views::filter keeps the items that pass a test. Its test function is called a predicate. Here x > 1 keeps only source values greater than one.
std::views::transform changes each kept value as it is read. Here it multiplies by ten. The | symbols connect the filtering and transforming steps in order.
The program prints 20 30, with a space after each number. Two and three pass the filter, then become twenty and thirty. The original vector still holds one, two, and three.
This view refers to values, so that vector must stay alive while the view uses it. The view is not a saved collection of answers. Do not return this view if its local source vector will be destroyed.
